title: The dualizing complex of a smooth scheme, for Weil complexes
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field, let $k$ be an algebraic closure of $k_0$, let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ be a prime, and put $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme whose structure morphism $a_0:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a:X\to s$. Write $\mathrm{WC}(X_0)=D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,\Lambda)$ for the category of Frobenius-fixed pairs $(K,\theta: Lg_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with $g_X$ geometric Frobenius. Use the equivariant compact-support functor $Ra_{0!}:\mathrm{WC}(X_0)\to\mathrm{WC}(\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$ of [prop-weil-operations]. Assume it has a right adjoint $Ra_0^!$, and define $\omega_{X_0}=Ra_0^!(\Lambda_s,\theta_0)$, where $(\Lambda_s,\theta_0)$ is the constant Weil sheaf of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. Then there is an isomorphism in $\mathrm{WC}(X_0)$
$$
\omega_{X_0}\ \cong\ \Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$
Here the target is the Tate twist by $d$ of the constant Weil sheaf on $X_0$, placed in degree zero and then shifted by $2d$; its Weil structure is the canonical one of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Shifting a fixed pair means shifting its underlying complex and its Frobenius isomorphism using the pullback-shift comparison; no triangulated structure on the fixed-pair category is asserted.

Mathlib DerivedCategory.exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE gives an isomorphism with singleFunctor b applied to some sheaf A.

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-weil-smooth-dualizing-cohomology with the same adjunction. Apply homologyFunctor b to the preceding isomorphism and use singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso to identify A with the degree b cohomology sheaf, then with the native Tate line tensor constant. Map this sheaf isomorphism through singleFunctor b. The singleFunctors shift comparison identifies this with the degree-zero tensor sheaf shifted by 2d. Lift the ambient isomorphism through the full native bounded constructible subcategory, using its inclusion-shift comparison.

proof.text: The native tensor by the lisse Tate line is right derivation of ihom from its dual. That ihom is exact, so singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso identifies tensoring a degree-zero constant complex with the degree-zero native tensor sheaf. Shift its inverse by 2d and compose. This yields precisely nonempty_dualizingComplex_iso; no equivalence between derived Weil sheaves and fixed pairs of derived objects is used.

lean.statement:
theorem nonempty_dualizingComplex_iso (d : ℕ)
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] :
    Nonempty (dualizingComplex k₀ l X ≅
      ((tateTwist k₀ l X d).obj
        (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj (WeilSheaf.adicConstant k₀ l X)))⟦(2 * d : ℤ)⟧) :=
  sorry
